name: Prochorus
overview: Prochorus is a male figure in the early Christian community, known primarily for being chosen to serve the widows of the Hellenistic Jews. This role highlights his service-oriented character within the church as recorded in Acts 6:5. No additional tribal or personal notes are provided.
namesAndTitles: The name Prochorus appears as a proper name in the Scriptures without a given meaning or divine origin noted. It is simply the personal name by which he is identified in Acts 6:5.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Prochorus beyond his role in serving the widows of the Hellenistic Jews. No other relational details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Prochorus holds significance as one of the early servants appointed to address the practical needs of the church, specifically caring for the widows among the Hellenistic Jewish believers. His selection reflects the early church's commitment to orderly ministry and compassionate service, ensuring that all members, especially vulnerable widows, were cared for in the growing Christian community.
